newsitem.title: USA: Bonneville offers power during heavy-load hours.
newsitem.headline: Bonneville offers power during heavy-load hours.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration expanded its offers for next-day, pre-scheduled power to heavy-load, as well as light-load, hours on both Sunday and Monday, the agency said Friday.
"Even though demand isn't that great, we are putting some feelers out there," said a trader at Bonneville.
"People are offering us power, so we thought we might as well be out in the market too."
Sales volume was limited to 600 megawatts for hours ending 0800 and 2400 PDT on Sunday, and from 0600 to 2400 on Monday.
The Portland, Ore.-based agency had declined to offer any power during peak-demand hours for most of this week.

For Sunday, Bonneville offered both firm and non-firm power between 0100 and 0800 and the hour ending 2400 PDT at $13.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), unchanged from earlier this week. Electricity between 0900 and 2300 is offered at $16.00.
For Monday, price offers were $20.00 during 1000-2000 PDT, $18.00 for 0700-0900 and 2200-2300, $15.00 for the hour ending 2400 and $13.00 for hours 0100 through 0600.
Bonneville also offered Northwest-only power during early morning hours at $9.00 on both Sunday and Monday.
